name: Es Campament penal colony, La Savina (Formentera)
story: After the war the Franco regime set up a penal colony for Republican prisoners on Formentera, beside the road from La Savina to La Mola. Some 2,133 men passed through it, many of them from mainland Spain and the Canaries. On 1 January 1942 it held 1,209 prisoners, on an island of about 3,000 inhabitants. At least 58 died of hunger and disease between 1941 and its closure in November 1942, and they were buried in Sant Francesc cemetery, where the Fòrum per la Memòria has exhumed remains. The site was declared a Bien de Interés Cultural in 2014, and the protection was upheld in court in 2018.
see: Low perimeter walls, barracks foundations, wells and a plaque with Joan Coromines' poem 'The Cemetery of the Living', beside the main road near the Estany des Peix.
plan: Seen from the PM-820 about 1 km out of La Savina port. Remains are fragmentary and luxury flats stand next to it, so stay on public land.

boxes.text: view it from the road or public path only.
Sources give 1,400 as the usual capacity and 2,133 as the total number who passed through; do not confuse the two figures.
